projects.title: AI Support Triage — a production agent
projects.summary: An agent that took over support-ticket triage and ran the full loop in production, with human sign-off.
projects.description: An agent that took over support-ticket triage: it classifies and routes each ticket, then a gated investigator agent reads the live system, code, telemetry, and docs to draft the fix and the reply — with a human approving every action.

sections.title: What I built
sections.body: I spearheaded an AI agent to take over support-ticket triage, work that was consuming roughly one in seven hours of the team's time. It runs the full loop in production: classify the ticket, investigate the live system, then draft the fix and the reply, with a human signing off on every action.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body:
A classifier handles and routes each ticket; a gated investigator agent then reads the live system, code, telemetry, and docs to draft a fix and a reply. A human approves every call before anything goes out. It was trained on two years of resolved history and improves with every correction.

@[System architecture — the agent, its gates, and the systems it reads (illustrative, clean-room)](/demo/20260803/assets/rr-triage-architecture.html)

![Claim → triage → spec flow: intake fills the queue, claiming labels the ticket, the agent runs against the rulebook, and a structured spec is written back — with a human gate on every write.](/demo/20260803/assets/portfolio/d-ai-triage/claim-to-spec-flow.png)

sections.title: Results
sections.body:
- **83.5%** handling accuracy on golden-set evals
- Routing accuracy **54% → 76%**
- Reclaimed roughly **one in seven hours** of team time, with a human in control
- Reached a team-wide, month-long production beta running the full loop

projects.title: Image Publishing Platform
projects.summary: A dynamic image-template platform powering automated social posts and personalized share artifacts.
projects.description: One image-generation platform, applied in three steps: a server-side rendering engine, a shipped consumer feature built on it, and a self-service concept to make it a paved road for any team.

sections.title: 1 · Dynamic Image-Template Platform
sections.body:
Server-side React templates rendered headlessly into composited share images at scale — the engine behind automated social posts and personalized quiz share cards. I owned it end to end, from the rendering engine to the template authoring model, then made it a turnkey path any team could adopt. Templates are data-driven, so one template produces a personalized artifact per post or per quiz taker.

![Dynamic template output](/demo/20260803/assets/portfolio/a-pubhub-templates/3.png)

![Admin / preview tool — pick a template, fill the fields, preview before it ships](/demo/20260803/assets/portfolio/a-pubhub-templates/1.png)

sections.title: 2 · Tag Yourself
sections.body:
The shipped consumer feature built on that engine: quiz results become personalized, generated share cards. Each card is personalized per quiz taker and built to earn the click before it reveals the result; the link pulls a friend back into the quiz, starting the loop again. It won its A/B test decisively.

![Personalized result share card](/demo/20260803/assets/portfolio/b-tag-yourself/product-result-page.png)

![The share loop: result → personalized card → a friend taps back in](/demo/20260803/assets/portfolio/b-tag-yourself/share-flow.png)

sections.title: 3 · Turnkey Sharing
sections.body:
A concept I designed to turn the proven share pattern into a paved road: one shared system, a small per-game config, and a self-service path so any game could add personalized sharing without a bespoke, multi-repo integration. An agent in the editor detects a shareable result and offers to wire the whole flow, no engineering ticket required. (My own concept and designs, shown as a proposal.)

![One system applied under every game's own skin](/demo/20260803/assets/portfolio/c-turn-key-sharing/pattern.png)

![Discovery → qualification → adoption, lowering friction at each stage](/demo/20260803/assets/portfolio/c-turn-key-sharing/discovery-flow.png)

sections.title: Results
sections.body:
- Tag Yourself won its A/B test: **+176%** desktop share engagement, **+82%** mobile web
- Return via shared links rose **59% → 69%**
- Became the shared engine behind automated posts and personalized cards; self-service let teams ship their own artifacts without routing through my team

projects.description: Designed an agent loop that migrated a decade-old Python UI service to Next.js — it self-verified every change, paused only at real blockers, and logged every decision.

media.description: The modernized Next.js result.

media.description: Filters and views in the migrated Next.js app.

sections.title: What I built
sections.body: I pioneered an agentic framework migration of a decade-old Python app to Next.js. I designed the agent loop that did the work: it self-verified every change, paused only at real blockers, and logged every decision.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The loop makes a change, verifies it against the test suite, and moves on, escalating to a human only at a genuine blocker. I packaged the whole approach as a reusable blueprint so it could be applied across similar systems rather than re-solved each time.

sections.title: Results
sections.body:
- **~70,000 lines** migrated in **~8%** of the estimated engineering time
- Test coverage **26% → 97%**
- Became the first reusable pattern, applied across **12+ services**
- Self-verifying loop with a human gate at real blockers only
